newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, no recovery expected soon.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, no recovery expected soon.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed on Tuesday on soaring volume and turnover with marginal price movements for most of the blue chips.
"Significant recovery (of the market) is not expected before Christmas," one market participant said, adding that fully listed drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka should remain unaffected.
"Some share prices have dropped so much that this is the right time to purchase," she said, mentioning food processor Podravka as one of the bargains.
Three of seven active issues were up, two were down and two flat. Volume almost tripled to 11,084 shares, while turnover rose to 11.1 million kuna.
Top gainer Privredna Banka rose to 250 from 145 kuna on volume of 100 shares, trading for the first time since September. The bank has been given the green light for rehabilitation by the government.
Most actively traded issue Zagrebacka Banka was also among gainers, adding 10 kuna to 990 with 8,000 units sold.
Chocolate maker Kras also rose, up three kuna to 405 on volume of 160 shares.
Bigger of the two losers hotelier Jadranturist edged down five kuna to 205 selling 178 shares. Podravka was down at 207 from 210 kuna with 2,141 shares changing hands.
Pliva and hotelier Suncani Hvar remained flat at 13,000 and 50 kuna respectively. Pliva sold 200 shares, while 305 Suncani Hvar shares were traded.
Second tranche of public debt refinancing bonds traded at 7.50 above par, compared to 7.15 on Friday on total turnover of 4.2 million kuna.
